title: Path tracing, BVH and denoising
summary: Explore acceleration structures, progressive raytracing and denoising as an alternative image pipeline.

blocks.text: RenderConfig.raytraceEnabled selects the compute-based path tracing pipeline. Entity RT_ENABLE determines participation in the relevant geometry path. RaytraceManager gathers compatible meshes, builds or updates acceleration structures, allocates geometry/material arenas and manages accumulation.

This is GPU compute path tracing through WebGPU. It does not expose a WebGPU hardware ray-tracing API or guarantee the use of vendor RT cores. “Hardware accelerated” in older notes means execution on the GPU.

BLAS stores local mesh acceleration data; TLAS references transformed instances. BVH construction supports spatial and SAH strategies. Geometry/topology updates and transform-only updates have different rebuild costs. Changing camera, lights, materials or geometry should invalidate accumulated samples when the represented image changes.

rtSamples sets per-frame sampling and rtMaxAccumulation controls accumulation limits. bounce_count, gamma and environment lighting affect the final image. A high sample count reduces stochastic noise at additional cost; check thin geometry and glass at the final resolution rather than only a static preview.

blocks.text: OIDN expects compatible HDR/color, albedo and normal channels and a supported model name. Native mode additionally requires external executables. Denoising can blur small detail when inputs or sample quality are poor; compare a reference crop before using it for technical lines and labels.
Explore the implementation in a scene
Hold camera, lighting and material fixed and let the image accumulate. Then move one object to see why a changed scene must invalidate accumulated samples.
